outcome.answer:
Different retraction maps can change spherical residual stability mainly by changing how update size becomes a rotation angle, not by changing norm preservation itself [1]. The exponential map is only one choice; the metric projection and Cayley retractions are exactly norm-preserving and appear to be more favorable in the reported experiments, with the best validation loss occurring at finite p rather than at the exponential-map limit [1].

More broadly, the paper says all retractions on the hypersphere collapse to a single scalar design choice, so the stability difference is in angular behavior: some retractions saturate their rotation angle instead of letting it grow without bound [1]. That makes the exponential map just one end of a spectrum, while Proj-SpheretNorm and Cay-SpheretNorm are finite-angle alternatives that still keep the residual stream on the sphere [1].
